patterns.note: Asymmetrical two-column hero with text on a light background and a full-bleed image on the right.
Strategic use of a classic serif font for emphasis within a predominantly sans-serif typography system, creating an editorial and sophisticated tone.
A muted, warm off-white background serves as a canvas for vibrant, brand-specific accent colors (red, green, blue) used sparingly for highlights and interactive elements.
Scroll-triggered reveals for content sections, where elements like service items and testimonials fade and slide into view sequentially.
The hero image employs a subtle parallax effect, moving slower than the scroll to add depth and visual interest.

technique_notes: A full-bleed hero image on the right side of the screen is paired with a light background on the left for textual content, and the image itself uses a subtle parallax effect, moving at a slower rate than the page scroll.
A transparent navigation bar remains fixed at the top of the viewport after initial scroll, maintaining its original styling without shrinking or gaining a background.

Content sections and their internal elements, such as service list items and testimonial blocks, are revealed with a staggered fade-up animation as they enter the viewport, orchestrated using GSAP ScrollTrigger.

design_tokens.type_scale: Balanced headings (~3x body) with a clear hierarchy, complemented by a distinctive serif for emphasis and large, light-weight uppercase labels.
design_tokens.radius: Subtle (minimal rounding on interactive elements, mostly sharp edges).
design_tokens.spacing: Airy (generous vertical spacing between sections and within content blocks, especially in the hero and service list).

standout: The site stands out with its sophisticated blend of a minimalist, airy layout and a carefully curated, vibrant accent color palette. The use of a classic serif font for key phrases against a modern sans-serif creates an editorial feel, while the subtle scroll-triggered animations add a layer of polish without being distracting.
